evidence: migrations/versions/b72d4946fb3c_added_view_edit_for_nsf_account.py:33-36 inserts ADMIN/NSF_SUSPENDED 'edit' and 'view'; 1c958b749a20_org_status_added_to_authorisation_view.py:147-148 inserts ADMIN/NSF_SUSPENDED 'make_payment' and 'generate_invoice'. No later migration deletes them (a490b2db8b13 only adds change_pad_info).

said: The reduced set generally has no edit or make_payment. For a suspended account, legal-api's authorized(['edit']) fails and returns 401.
evidence: True for non-admin members (no NSF_SUSPENDED rows for COORDINATOR/USER), but ADMIN keeps edit/view (b72d4946fb3c:33-36) and make_payment (1c958b749a20:147), so an NSF admin passes the edit check; the claim is wrong for ADMIN.

said: PaymentLineItem.create raises FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED (401) when waived_fee_amount > 0 and user lacks STAFF; invoice rolled back.
evidence: services/payment_line_item.py:300-304 'if fee.waived_fee_amount > 0: if user.has_role(Role.STAFF.value): ... else: raise BusinessException(Error.FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED)'; called from payment_service.py:119 in the invoice path; errors.py:48 maps it to 401; payment_service.py except block calls invoice.rollback() and re-raises. fee_schedule.py:165-167 fee_amount setter sets _waived_fee_amount = fee+priority+future when fee zeroed and not variable, and waive_fees (fee_schedule.py:319-323) zeroes fee_amount, so a non-staff waiveFees on a fixed non-zero fee yields waived>0 and is rejected. Gaps: zero-fee filings (waived=0) and variable-fee schedules (setter skips because _variable; _calculate_fees then resets fee_amount to the requested fee, payment_service.py:~315) are not rejected; their priority/future/service fees are still zeroed silently.
reference_fix: The fee-quote endpoint honours waiveFees only for staff. On the invoice endpoint, FeeSchedule zeroes filing, priority, future-effective and service fees with no role check, but PaymentLineItem.create (payment_line_item.py:300-304) then raises FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED (401, invoice rolled back) for any non-staff caller when the waived amount is > 0. That covers fixed non-zero fees. Zero-fee and variable-fee schedules (waived amount stays 0) pass without any role check.

said: waiveFees on a normal fixed-fee filing: pay-api 401 FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED, shown by legal-api as 402. The saved filing is left unpaid.
evidence: Same payment_line_item.py:300-304 raise. legal-api business_filings.py create_invoice falls through to 'return {...unable to create invoice for payment.}, HTTPStatus.PAYMENT_REQUIRED' (line ~886) for non-200/201/400 responses; the filing was already saved before create_invoice (complete_filing), with no payment_token, so it stays a draft/unpaid. Reference fact 7's last sentence 'a regular user's waived-fee filing is processed without payment' only holds for zero-fee or variable-fee schedules.
reference_fix: Neither listener checks amount paid, waived fees or submitter role, so a filing whose invoice was created as $0 is processed without payment. For a regular user this only happens when the invoice itself succeeds (zero-fee or variable-fee schedules); waiveFees on a fixed non-zero fee is rejected by pay-api with 401 FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED (legal-api returns 402) and never reaches the listeners.

said: get_filing_types copies header.waiveFees and header.priority into every fee line for any caller.
evidence: business_filings.py:~716-722: courtOrder/registrarsNotation/registrarsOrder/putBackOn/adminFreeze entries contain only filingTypeCode and filingDescription; COOP affidavit and NOFEE entries get waiveFees but no priority (~705-712, 717). 'No role check' part is right.

said: Pay-api does not check the waive flag at all.
evidence: payment_line_item.py:300-304 raises FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED for non-staff when waived_fee_amount > 0; fee_schedule.py:319 and the fee_amount setter at :165-167 are only the zeroing step (no role check there). Also fee.py quote path checks staff. Reference fact 5 is itself overstated on 'no role check' (see reference_fix).
reference_fix: The fee-quote endpoint honours waiveFees only when the token has the staff role. On the invoice endpoint, FeeSchedule zeroes filing, priority, future-effective and service fees with no role check, but PaymentLineItem.create (payment_line_item.py:300-304) raises FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED (401) for non-staff when the resulting waived amount is > 0 (fixed non-zero fees). Zero-fee and variable-fee schedules slip through.

said: copies filing/header/waiveFees into every filingTypes[].waiveFees entry with no role check
evidence: No role check: right. 'Every entry': wrong; business_filings.py get_filing_types branch for ['courtOrder','registrarsNotation','registrarsOrder','putBackOn','adminFreeze'] appends only filingTypeCode and filingDescription, no waiveFees. Overstated rather than contradicted on the role point.

said: get_filing_types copies filing/header/waiveFees into each filingTypes entry without looking at the role.
evidence: Same: staff-only filing types (courtOrder, registrarsNotation, registrarsOrder, putBackOn, adminFreeze) get no waiveFees. 'Without role check' is right; 'each entry' is overstated.

said: entity-pay worker then sees the payment as completed and marks the filing paid.
evidence: entity_pay/worker.py:114-117 only sets filing_submission.payment_completion_date and commits (and publishes a PAID email message); it never assigns status. But legal-api models/filing.py:1198-1199 before-flush listener 'elif filing.payment_completion_date ...: filing._status = Filing.Status.PAID.value' derives PAID on commit, so the filing does end up PAID. Reference ('does not set PAID explicitly') is accurate about the worker; the claim is right about the effect.
